Une journée d'étude dédiée à la préventi: A study day dedicated to the prevention of corruption in public procurement was organized by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, in collaboration with the High Authority for Transparency, Prevention and Fight against Corruption (HATPLC). The event, marked by the presence of senior officials, aims to regulate procurement procedures in the telecom sector, a strategic field for Algeria where Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo play a key role.
Alger, 11 juin 2026 – Le ministère de la: Algiers, June 11, 2026 – The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, led by Minister Sid Ali Zerrouki, organized a study day under the theme "Prevention of corruption during the preparation phase of public procurement." The event, held in the presence of Ms. Salima Mousserati, President of the HATPLC, is part of a global approach aimed at establishing a culture of transparency and fairness in the management of public equipment, particularly in the telecom sector.
Un cadre juridique renforcé pour les mar: A reinforced legal framework for public procurement
Cette initiative s'appuie sur l'introduc: This initiative relies on the introduction of a strict legal and regulatory framework, designed to govern procurement procedures and guarantee fair competition among economic operators. In a sector as strategic as telecoms, where public investments are colossal, the fight against corruption becomes an imperative to ensure efficient public spending and protect state funds.
Les discussions ont porté sur les risque: Discussions focused on corruption risks related to the needs identification phase and the drafting of specifications, two critical stages in procurement preparation. Participants, including experts, representatives of regulatory bodies and ministry executives, exchanged views on prevention mechanisms and the central role of transparency in improving the business climate.
Mobilis, Djezzy et Ooredoo dans la ligne: Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo in the crosshairs
Le secteur des télécoms en Algérie, domi: The telecom sector in Algeria, dominated by the three historical operators – Mobilis (Algérie Télécom), Djezzy (Orascom Telecom Algérie) and Ooredoo Algeria – is fertile ground for transparency issues. Public procurement in this area notably concerns the acquisition of network equipment, 5G licenses, or even fiber optic infrastructures. Opaque management of these contracts could distort competition and penalize operators, while burdening public finances.
La journée d'étude a ciblé les cadres ce: The study day targeted central ministry executives, officials of affiliated public economic institutions, as well as members of procurement committees. Local officials also participated via video conferences, emphasizing the importance of a decentralized approach to ensure the application of new standards.
Les meilleures pratiques internationales: International best practices in corruption prevention were presented, with a particular focus on compliance with competition rules and equality among operators. The objective is twofold: to strengthen the efficiency of public spending and protect the money of Algerians.
Cette initiative s'aligne sur les réform: This initiative aligns with ongoing reforms in the telecom sector, where Algeria seeks to modernize its infrastructure while ensuring sound and transparent management. This is a priority for a country where telecom represents a major economic driver, as well as a sector sensitive to the risks of malpractice.
